title: Guess a Formula! Dimensions Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A park swing, a clock pendulum and a lab bob all swing in a fixed time. What decides that time? Aarav ties his keys to a string in the college corridor and, with no formula and no textbook, finds the form of the answer using only dimensions. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn the three uses of dimensional analysis: checking a formula, converting units and building a formula.

A live pendulum simulation runs beside its angle-time graph with a slow-mo replay of the gravity and velocity vectors. We guess T = k m^x l^y g^z and match the powers of M, L and T step by step to get T = k sqrt(l/g), then read what each power means: mass does not matter, T grows as the square root of the length, and stronger gravity means a faster swing. Two pause-and-think questions test the square root rule and the conversion ratio. Then a worked example (how many ergs make one joule), the exam trap about newtons and dynes, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
